fixes.explanation: No warning in sight, friend. Laban says, “I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you.” That's the opposite of bad news. He's telling Jacob the blessing came with Jacob's name on it. And right after, he says, “Name your wages…” That's not how anybody talks when they've just been warned.

Jacob's sons are a good guess, but the text says Laban put the animals “…under the care of his sons.” That's Laban's own household. Then he puts a three-day journey between himself and Jacob (Genesis 30:36). Three days! I've had a longer trip to find the one good spatula in my kitchen. I think those animals just got a very quiet new neighborhood.

problems.problem: Saying Laban checked his books and found Jacob's name in the numbers adds an action the text does not give. Laban says he learned by divination.
The cookie comparison suggests Laban put the animals in his sons' care so Jacob could not reach them. The passage does not state that reason.
